claim: Greshake et al. named and systematized indirect prompt injection, with a taxonomy including data theft, worming, and information ecosystem contamination.

source.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection

evidence_quote: LLM-Integrated Applications blur the line between data and instructions

claim: OWASP LLM01:2025 distinguishes direct prompt injection (user's own prompt) from indirect prompt injection (external content like websites/files altering model behavior).
evidence_quote: Direct prompt injections occur when a user's prompt input directly alters the behavior of the model

claim: A 2025 study on hidden-content injection for web agents enumerates five concrete hiding techniques: HTML comments, data attributes, CSS-hidden text, hidden form fields, and semantic attribute abuse.

source.title: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents

evidence_quote: five hidden strategies include HTML comments, data attributes, CSS-hidden text, form hidden fields, and semantic attribute abuse

claim: Observed real-world indirect prompt injection has used base64-encoded payloads decoded at runtime into off-screen DOM elements with timed delays to evade time-bounded safety scans.

source.title: Fooling AI Agents: Web-Based Indirect Prompt Injection Observed in the Wild

evidence_quote: Base64-encoded instructions are decoded at runtime and inserted as off-screen, invisible DOM elements

claim: A GCG-optimized universal adversarial trigger embedded in HTML accessibility-tree elements achieves high attack success against a BrowserGym agent powered by Llama-3.1, though exact ASR/sample size were not confirmed.

source.title: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree

evidence_quote: high success rates across real websites in both targeted and general attacks

claim: InjecAgent (1,054 test cases, 17 user tools, 62 attacker tools) found ReAct-prompted GPT-4 vulnerable to indirect prompt injection 24% of the time, rising to 47% under an enhanced hacking-style setting.

source.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents

evidence_quote: ReAct-prompted GPT-4 is vulnerable to attacks 24% of the time

claim: Agent Security Bench (10 scenarios, 10 agents, 400+ tools, 27 attack/defense methods, 13 LLM backbones) reports a highest average attack success rate of 84.30%, with tested defenses showing limited effectiveness.

source.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents

evidence_quote: highest average attack success rate of 84.30%, but limited effectiveness shown in current defenses

claim: A paper on adaptive attacks breaking published indirect prompt injection defenses on LLM agents exists on arXiv, but specific numeric results could not be extracted from the fetched PDF.

source.title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents

evidence_quote: title and existence confirmed via arXiv listing; PDF did not parse cleanly for numeric details

claim: Task drift is defined as the LLM's deviation from the user's original instructions after processing external data; a linear probe on activation deltas achieves ROC AUC greater than 0.99 on a 500,000+ instance dataset, outperforming Prompt Guard (0.974) and Prompt Shields (0.988) on the authors' own test set.

source.title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas

evidence_quote: the LLM's deviation from the user's original instruction(s)

claim: WASP separates ASR-intermediate (agent begins following injected instruction, 16-86% across agents/scenarios) from ASR-end-to-end (attacker's full goal achieved, only 0-17%), showing partial hijacking is common but full goal completion is rare.

source.title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks

evidence_quote: agents begin executing the adversarial instruction between 16 and 86% but only achieve the goal between 0 and 17%

claim: An empirical study across four VLMs (including GPT-4o and Claude), twelve font sizes, and ten image transformations found multimodal text-image embedding distance strongly predicts typographic prompt-injection attack success, with rendering conditions swinging ASR by tens of percentage points.

source.title: Reading Between the Pixels: Linking Text-Image Embedding Alignment to Typographic Attack Success on Vision-Language Models

evidence_quote: multimodal embedding distance strongly predicts attack success rate

claim: A 2026 SoK synthesizes more than 20 prior studies into a taxonomy of agentic AI attack surfaces spanning prompt-level injection, RAG/knowledge-base poisoning, tool/plugin exploits, and multi-agent manipulation.

source.title: SoK: The Attack Surface of Agentic AI -- Tools and Autonomy

evidence_quote: develops a comprehensive taxonomy of attacks spanning prompt-level injections, knowledge-base poisoning, tool/plug-in exploits
